key_insight: SGD induces teacher-dependent spectral spikes outside the teacher subspace, amplifying representation variance and degrading generalization.
engineering_relevance: Controlling feature updates outside task-relevant directions may improve generalization in neural networks.
method: Decompose first-layer weights into teacher-aligned and orthogonal components.
Analyze joint SGD dynamics with the second layer in the proportional limit.
Introduce Decomposed Dynamics, a tractable surrogate matching SGD’s asymptotic test-error dynamics.
evidence_signal: ReLU-student simulations show better generalization when orthogonal-complement directions are frozen rather than trained.
watch_item: The analysis concerns two-layer networks and a multi-index teacher model; applicability to deeper networks and real-world data remains unestablished.
paper_title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
